{{Short description|Class equipped with a preorder}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''preordered class''' is a [[class (mathematics)|class]] equipped with a [[preorder]].

==Definition==
When dealing with a class ''C'', it is possible to define a class relation on ''C'' as a [[Subclass (set theory)|subclass]] of the power class ''C <math> \times </math> C'' . Then, it is convenient to use the language of [[relation (mathematics)|relations]] on a set.

A '''preordered class''' is a class with a [[preorder]] on it. ''Partially ordered class'' and ''totally ordered class'' are defined in a similar way. These concepts  generalize respectively those of [[preordered set]], [[partially ordered set]] and [[totally ordered set]]. However, it is difficult to work with them as in the ''small'' case because many constructions common in a [[set theory]] are no longer possible in this framework.

Equivalently, a preordered class is a '''[[thin category]]''', that is, a [[category (mathematics)|category]] with at most one morphism from an object to another.

==Examples==
*In any [[category (mathematics)|category]] ''C'', when ''D'' is a class of morphisms of ''C'' containing identities and closed under composition, the relation 'there exists a ''D''-morphism from ''X'' to ''Y''' is a preorder on the class of objects of ''C''.
*The class '''Ord''' of all [[ordinal number|ordinal]]s is a totally ordered class with the classical ordering of ordinals.
